title: Adversarial synthetic probes + explainable regression attribution for golden-set gating
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:
We currently gate canary and shadow rollouts using static golden prompt scorecards and threshold checks. These gates are effective for surface-level semantic regressions but miss targeted regressions caused by subtle token-level or distributional shifts (e.g., hallucination stems triggered by adversarial inputs or prompt boundary tokenization changes). We need tooling that proactively finds weak points in the model via adversarial/synthetic probes derived from golden sets and then surfaces explainable attribution so engineers and PMs can quickly decide: rollback, quarantine, or patch and continue the rollout.

Proposal:
1) Generate a set of adversarial synthetic probes for each golden prompt set. Probes include token perturbations, paraphrase variants, and targeted context-shift templates (language-agnostic where relevant). Probes are weighted by likelihood of occurrence and customer impact (derived from traffic cohorts).
2) Execute probes in pre-rollout staging and in shadow traffic. Collect per-probe metrics (semantic score delta, hallucination probability, length/termination anomalies, beam diversity collapse).
3) Compute an explainable regression attribution report per canary: which probes and which token spans contributed most to metric degradation, with simple heuristics (attention-focused token saliency + logit-delta fingerprints).
4) Integrate with the existing gating system to allow automated quarantine triggers based on probe-weighted risk score and expose a human-in-the-loop adjudication UI with suggested actions and confidence bands.

Scope and deliverables:
- Synthetic probe generator service (deterministic templates + random seed modes) and probe catalog storage.
- Probe execution hook in shadow/canary harness with sampling configuration per cohort.
- Explainability pipeline producing per-probe attribution artifacts (token spans, saliency scores, example diffs).
- New gating rule type: probe-weighted quarantine that can be parameterized per-customer cohort and model variant.
- Console UI/Runbook integration for human adjudication, plus auto-quarantine automation policy with hysteresis.

Why this is different from existing work:
Many existing tickets focus on aggregate scorecards and probabilistic gating. This work augments those signals with adversarially crafted probes and deterministic attribution so that when a gate trips we can immediately point to the offending input variations and provide actionable remediation guidance (rollback, targeted patch prompts, tokenizer fixes, or model re-quantization checks).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Synthetic probe generator produces at least 200 unique probes for three pilot golden sets (chat completion, summarization, instruction follow).
2) Probe execution integrated into the shadow harness; probe traffic runs in-situ with real shadow traffic without exceeding 0.2% extra token-cost budget in pilot accounts.
3) Attribution reports correctly surface top-3 probe causes for an injected regression simulation (we will run a regression emulator to validate).
4) New gating policy available in Console that can trigger an auto-quarantine action and provides the explainability report link in the quarantine alert.
5) Pilot rollout executed for two internal customers with documented adjudication steps and a postmortem describing actions taken.
comments: 2025-02-15 - Maya Chen: Initial write-up and proposal. Shared with PM and Reliability teams. Asked for prioritization and a pilot cohort. Linked design brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/R/Adversarial+Probes+Design

2025-02-18 - Alejandro Ruiz: Spike complete for probe generator. Found that simple token deletions + verb tense swaps already surface regressions in the summarization golden set; captured prototype scripts in runtime repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6812

2025-02-20 - Priya Nambiar (PM): Reviewed approach; requested that probe weighting include customer signal (frequency and revenue bucket). Added to acceptance criteria. Also asked for explicit fallback policy for false positives.

2025-02-22 - Design review (Lena Park): Console needs a condensed explanation card (top offending probes) + expandable technical detail. Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleDesignLink

2025-02-25 - Reliability (Ben Ortiz): Measured overhead of probe execution in a staging cluster. Median latency impact is <3% for sample sizes up to 500 probes per minute. Recommend starting pilot with 50 probes/min per cohort.

2025-02-28 - Alejandro Ruiz: Implemented prototype attribution algorithm (logit-delta + attention saliency). Early results look promising — produced human-readable spans in 82% of simulated regressions. Pushed PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6847
notes: Next steps: finalize probe taxonomy, agree on default weighting heuristics with Growth/Revenue, schedule pilot with two internal CS teams. If gating proves noisy, add quick-dispatch operator flow for manual quarantine override.
